transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, occupational health at the department sent me. They're saying I'm not eating enough. I mean, most days I just keep it to black coffee... maybe a plain yogurt or a few bites of chicken at night. Sitting down for a full meal just feels like I'm letting my standards slip.
Are you afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yeah, I am. If I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this jolt... like I've just completely lost control of things. When that happens, I'll spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder. I just really can't stand the idea of putting any weight back on.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?

I'm about 5 foot 10. As for my weight... well, when the nurse weighed me just before I came in here, she told me it was dangerously low. 

I mean, I know it's gone down. My uniform hangs off me now, and I've had to tighten my duty belt past all the old notches just to keep it on. But honestly, even when she said the number was dangerous, I still just thought to myself that I could stand to be a little sharper.
Do you ever make yourself throw up, or use things like laxatives or water pills to keep your weight down?
No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself sick or take any pills or laxatives. I just control what I eat.

There is no evidence of binge-eating or purging behavior, consistent with Anorexia Nervosa (restricting type).
